scope: The rule paraphrases and exact ISO locators below were checked against the locally supplied ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text (ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.txt): PDF string-decoding/spacing interfaces, supported font dictionaries and embedding bindings, character selection, widths/CID metrics, PDF-specific CMap rules and ToUnicode. Every code-to-name slot of Standard, MacRoman, WinAnsi, PDFDoc, Symbol and ZapfDingbats was compared with Annex D; MacExpert was also checked. This is not verification of Adobe Glyph List rules, TN5014 grammar or external font-program binary formats. Provider additions were checked against ISO 9.6.2.2/Table 109 and 9.9.2, 9.8.1-9.8.2/Tables 120-121, 9.7.5.2/Table 116 and 9.10.2, and TN5014 sections 5.1-5.4 for pinned resource inheritance. AFM values and Unicode projection choices are checked against the pinned data files, not claimed as verification of external AFM or sfnt format standards. Recovery additions were checked against ISO 9.7.4.1 Table 115, 9.7.4.2, 9.7.5.4, 9.7.6.2, 9.10.3 and TN5014 7.4. Tolerant interpretations depart from those rules as individually reported below; corpus acceptance is evidence of tolerance, not standards conformance. Round 5 rechecks the PDF TrueType routes against 9.6.5.4 and Table 113 in the same local ISO text; final-paragraph alternatives are reader policy. Retained byte accounting is ADR 0012 policy, not a numerical requirement of Annex C.1. Substitution and optional-weight handling were checked against ISO 9.6.2.1-9.6.2.2, 9.6.5.2, 9.6.5.4, 9.8.1-9.8.2/Tables 120-121 and 9.9.2 in the same local text. Sixty-six Russian AFII name-to-scalar records were compared with local adobe-glyph-list data. Short aliases and invalid-weight discard are documented policies; full external AGL/AGLFN algorithm verification is not claimed. Horizontal CID substitution and Symbol/Dingbats additions were checked against the same local ISO text: 9.6.2.2, 9.6.5.2/Table 112, 9.6.5.4, 9.7.3/Table 114, 9.7.4.2-9.7.4.3, 9.7.5 and 9.10.2-9.10.3. CFF INDEX, DICT, charset layouts and standard SIDs used by the Foxit oracle were checked against local TN5176 sections 4, 5, 8-10, 13-14 and Appendix A. Regional OTF cmap expectations are independent binary-layout oracles; primary OpenType format review remains pending. Collection projection, Unicode subtable preference, horizontal-only substitutes and coalesced coverage diagnostics are explicit provider policies.

verification.verdict: ISO subset agrees after corrections

Unrecognized name components contribute no Unicode, and entirely unknown names return None; this external AGL algorithm remains pending primary-text review.

requirements.status: Symbolic or unencoded fonts use direct symbol/Mac codes; encoded nonsymbolic fonts use names via Unicode, Mac OS Roman, then post.

verification.rule: Symbolic or unencoded fonts use direct symbol/Mac codes; encoded nonsymbolic fonts use names via Unicode, Mac OS Roman, then post.
verification.implementation: ISO selection routes implemented with distinct Windows BMP, full-Unicode and platform-0 API variants.

choices: When symbolic/no-Encoding wording overlaps the named/Nonsymbolic wording, the more specific direct-code paragraph takes precedence.

Use the prescribed name route and post before reader-chosen fallbacks. After failure try Mac OS Roman by glyph name, full Windows Unicode (3,10), platform 0 Unicode, then the symbol byte route. Never use ToUnicode to select a glyph.
The four allowed symbol high-byte ranges are tried in ascending order; a conforming symbol cmap uses one range.
When Mac OS Roman contains aliases for a name, the lowest character code is used.

For direct codes, try symbol high-byte variants, then Mac Roman. Only after failure try (3,1), (3,10), then platform 0; within each Unicode table try the literal byte before F000/F100/F200 offsets. Missing all routes selects glyph 0. Multi-scalar names never select a scalar cmap entry.
A successful post lookup is binding even for glyph 0; reader fallback applies only when lookup fails.

choices: Reject malformed extraction interpretations under Strict, report the rejection and discard the optional map while keeping the drawable font in both recovery modes. Other Unicode fallback methods remain available.
Repair two-byte simple-font source codes by their low byte, preserving agreeing aliases and dropping conflicting aliases.
Omit invalid UTF-16 destinations atomically, including malformed surrogate sequences and odd byte counts. An invalid child definition suppresses inherited text for that source.
Repair overflowing bfrange strings with big-endian byte carry. Keep valid UTF-16 results, omit invalid ones, and stop at full-string overflow without wrapping.
On other malformed, unsupported, cyclic or budget-exceeding ToUnicode data, discard the whole map and report font.tounicode-invalid. Existing parser and output budgets remain enforced.

Interpret an otherwise reversed byte bound as an integer interval, split into disjoint aligned rectangular pieces without widening it. Reversed whole intervals, conflicting codespaces and ambiguous code lengths remain errors.

requirements.status: PdfFont::retained_bytes is a saturating, constant-time retained-storage estimate computed once when loading succeeds (ADR 0012 policy).
requirements.gaps: No allocator telemetry or peak bound. Private FontProgram tables use an explicit proxy until pagura-font exposes a retained estimate; renderer admission is outside this crate.

verification.rule: Annex C.1 discusses processor limits; the retained accounting amounts and provider ownership convention are implementation policy under ADR 0012.
verification.implementation: Owned encoding payloads, widths, vertical metrics, CMaps, Unicode, CIDToGIDMap, Type 3 resources/procedures and an embedded-program proxy are computed once. Names include payload allowances; trees add 64 bytes per entry. Provider-owned shared resources are excluded and remain its cache-budget responsibility.
verification.expectations: Unit tests cover all five requested font categories, owned resource growth, stable repeated reads, shared provider identity/Unicode exclusion and saturating arithmetic. No allocator-accurate size is claimed.
verification.verdict: Accounting policy tested, not an ISO-defined byte count.
choices: Include the PdfFont struct itself, but exclude Document-owned source dictionaries/streams and renderer-owned outlines. Replace the renderer input-size estimate with retained_bytes; do not add the two.

Embedded private FontProgram storage uses two input byte lengths plus 192 bytes per glyph, 16 KiB fixed overhead, the public program struct and Arc headers. This models parsed offsets, charstrings, encodings and indexes without reparsing a program or walking glyphs.

Provider substitute programs, predefined CMaps and CID-to-Unicode tables are charged by their provider, never per font. Copied encodings/metrics, embedded maps and inherited map copies remain owned allocations.

repair_policy.behaviour: Discard unusable optional extraction data in both recovery modes; never change glyph selection.
In repair mode use low bytes of two-byte simple-font sources; conflicting aliases have unknown Unicode. Strict discards the rejected map.
In repair mode omit invalid destinations, retaining unaffected entries and blocking invalid child overrides from resurrecting parent values. Strict discards the rejected map.
In repair mode increment with big-endian carry, retaining valid destinations until full-string overflow; never wrap. Strict discards the rejected map.
Accept counts above 100 within existing budgets only after permission to repair.
Split malformed rectangular bounds into an exact integer interval, accepting only non-overlapping, unambiguous pieces.
Assume Identity when the required embedded Type2 CIDFont map is missing, after permission to repair.
While choosing an unknown non-embedded Latin face, report and ignore an invalid optional weight, preserving normal default 400 and independent descriptor flags. Strict rejects with the tag.
